raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through the way I always do.

---

I've been on this land 45 years, and I do things the way I know works. My 18 mu isn't all in one piece — the flat ground, about 12 mu, that's my wheat-maize ground. One crop follows the other, no rest, same as everyone in the village. The other 6 mu sits in cotton. It's been cotton ground long as I remember, and I know how to manage it.

I've got six mouths at home, but two of the young ones work in town now and send a little back. So it's mostly me and the wife working the fields, with the kids coming back to help at harvest when they can. That's how we get the cotton picked — no way to do it without them.

**Wheat.** I plant after the Cold Dew, usually middle of October when the heat's gone out of the ground. I use seed I saved from last year's crop — why would I buy it when my own wheat grows fine? Before I plant I have the tractor man run the rotary tiller over the stubble, and I spread compound fertilizer, close to one bag for every one-and-a-half mu. Then come spring when it stands up at jointing, I broadcast urea, about half a bag per mu. I water three times if the heavens don't help — once before winter so it doesn't die of thirst under the ice, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. The well water costs money to pump, so I don't water more than I have to. Last year I got maybe 400 kg per mu, about like always.

**Maize.** Right after I cut the wheat in June I've got to get the maize in fast — maybe three days, four at the most, or it won't finish before the cold. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, everybody does, can't save maize seed. I have the seeder man drop it straight into the wheat stubble. I put compound fertilizer in with the seed, and then when the maize is about knee-high I put on urea. I water once at tasseling if it's dry. Maize does better than wheat here — I usually get 450, sometimes 500 if the rain comes right.

**Cotton.** Cotton is more work and more money, but the price is usually worth it. I plow the cotton ground deep before planting, end of April. I buy seed every year from the shop — the good varieties the neighbors use. I put on compound fertilizer before planting and topdress urea when it starts to flower. Cotton gets bugs bad — I spray for bollworm maybe three or four times, sometimes more if it's a bad year. I watch the neighbors' fields too. Water once or twice if it's dry through July-August. Picking starts in September and goes into October, and the whole family comes back for that — kids, grandkids, everyone. Last year I got about 250 kg lint per mu.

Money's tight like always. I don't have cash to waste, so I don't put on more fertilizer than I need, but I don't skimp either — wheat looking yellow is worse than spending a little extra on a bag of urea.
